summary: Frontend-only visual verification of the Discover screen category-chip fixes. Logged in as demo consumer, cycled through all 7 categories (All/Music/Art/Tech/Food/Sports/Other) in BOTH dark (default) and light themes. Bug 1 (white-square inside active chip icon) is FIXED — every active chip renders a clean glyph with a colored border + accent halo, no white/solid rectangle artifact behind the icon on the web preview. Bug 2 (static header tint) is FIXED — the header LinearGradient wash now dynamically re-tints per category: All=red/pink, Music=purple, Art=orange, Tech=cyan, Food=red, Sports=teal, Other=slate. Regression checks pass: shelves (Featured / Free & popular / More near you) render with poster cards + ribbons + FREE badge, chip spring/wiggle animations play, tab bar & login flow unaffected, theme toggle in Profile flips dark<->light correctly. Note: Bug 1's Android-specific double-elevation artifact cannot be reproduced on Expo web preview (elevation is native-only) — the code-level fix (halo shadow/elevation moved to outer chipShadow wrapper only + transparent bg guard on icon animated wrapper) matches the RN #30039 workaround pattern and looks correct on inspection.

issues: CATEGORIES 'All' uses color '#EF4444' (red) — same hex as 'Food'. The review request specifies 'All pink #F84464' (brand pink). Result: when the user toggles between All and Food the header wash looks identical, and the 'All' halo doesn't match the brand pink. Recommend changing CATEGORIES[0].color from '#EF4444' to '#F84464' in /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:40 to match the spec.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warns 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow.' twice on app boot. Likely originating from shadows.card in /app/frontend/src/theme.ts (used by chipCard, posterShadow, etc.). RN Web / react-native >=0.76 now prefers boxShadow. Not blocking, but worth migrating in a follow-up. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:839 (chipCard uses ...shadows.card), :874 (posterShadow uses ...shadows.card).

Console warns 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Comes from the header <LinearGradient pointerEvents="none" /> at /app/frontend/app/(consumer)/discover.tsx:611. Move to style.pointerEvents to silence.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix implementation matches the described RN #30039 workaround: active accent halo (shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius/elevation=12) is only applied to the OUTER chipShadow wrapper (discover.tsx:176-186), and the inner chipCard keeps only the neutral `...shadows.card`. Icon's animated wrapper gets an explicit `backgroundColor: 'transparent'` (discover.tsx:191) as belt-and-suspenders. Looks correct.

headerTint computation (discover.tsx:594-600) properly derives rgba(r,g,b,0.22) from activeCategory.color and is memoised on `activeCategory`. LinearGradient at :606-612 consumes it and re-renders on category change — verified visually in dark and light themes.
activeCategory (discover.tsx:588-591) falls back to CATEGORIES[0] if the current key is unknown — safe.
chipShadow style (:824-828) intentionally has no static shadow — only the active state adds the halo. Good, prevents idle-state double-elevation.

rca_of_issue: Bug 1 RCA (accepted from main agent, verified against code): Previously both the outer wrapper (which already carried shadows.card) AND the inner chipCard applied active-state shadow* + elevation. On some Android GPUs, RN renders the second elevation layer as a solid rectangle behind the icon (RN issue #30039) — appearing as a white square because chipCard's background color for the active state is the accent + '1A' (~10% alpha) tint, which lets the underlying elevation rectangle bleed through as a light box. Fix: keep only chipShadow (outer wrapper) as the elevation source in the active state; leave chipCard with the neutral shadows.card only, plus explicit transparent bg on the icon's animated wrapper. Verified on web preview — no artifact and no visual regression across all 7 categories in dark + light. Bug 2 RCA: header LinearGradient was hard-coded to colors.brandTertiary. Fix: derive activeCategory from CATEGORIES and compute rgba(...,0.22) from its hex accent, then pass into the top-of-gradient stop. Verified visually — tint changes as expected on each category selection in both themes.
